item.text:
# Vladimir Putin, Russia, 2023: Initial Evidence Note

Question IDs below are broad inferred lenses, not repo-verified subquestion codes, because I did not inspect repository docs in this isolated pass.

## 2023 Events

1. **ICC arrest warrant for Putin**. `Publisher:` International Criminal Court; `Date:` 17 Mar 2023; `URL:` [icc-cpi.int/situations/ukraine](https://www.icc-cpi.int/situations/ukraine); `Summary:` The ICC announced arrest warrants for Vladimir Putin and Maria Lvova-Belova over the alleged unlawful deportation and transfer of Ukrainian children. This is the clearest 2023 legal indictment of Putin’s wartime conduct. `Question IDs:` `8B`, `7A`.

2. **Putin framed the Wagner mutiny as treason**. `Publisher:` Reuters Connect; `Date:` 24 Jun 2023; `URL:` [reutersconnect.com/item/moment-putin-says-wagner-mutiny-is-treason-in-televised-address](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/moment-putin-says-wagner-mutiny-is-treason-in-televised-address/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjM6bmV3c21sX1ZBMjQwMTI0MDYyMDIzUlAx); `Summary:` In a televised address, Putin called Wagner’s armed challenge “treason” and promised punishment. The episode showed a serious internal rupture in his 2023 rule, even though he survived it politically. `Question IDs:` `7A`, `8B`.

3. **Official 2023 human-rights reporting describes a deeper crackdown**. `Publisher:` U.S. Department of State; `Date:` 22 Apr 2024; `URL:` [state.gov/reports/2023-country-reports-on-human-rights-practices/russia](https://www.state.gov/reports/2023-country-reports-on-human-rights-practices/russia); `Summary:` The report says authorities used new laws to punish dissent and independent expression, jailed antiwar protesters and opposition figures, forced NGO closures, further restricted media, and intensified pressure on critics inside and outside Russia. This is strong background evidence for the character of Putin’s 2023 rule. `Question IDs:` `6A`, `7A`.

4. **Russia’s 2023 economy still grew**. `Publisher:` Rosstat; `Date:` 7 Feb 2024; `URL:` [rosstat.gov.ru/folder/313/document/230009](https://www.rosstat.gov.ru/folder/313/document/230009); `Summary:` Rosstat’s first 2023 estimate put GDP growth at 3.6% year over year. That supports a favorable reading on macroeconomic resilience despite sanctions and war. `Question IDs:` `8B`.

## Background / 2023 Context

5. **Putin’s approval stayed high after the mutiny**. `Publisher:` Levada Center; `Date:` 14 Jul 2023; `URL:` [levada.ru/en/2023/07/14/approval-of-institutions-ratings-of-politicians-and-parties-at-the-end-of-june-2023](https://www.levada.ru/en/2023/07/14/approval-of-institutions-ratings-of-politicians-and-parties-at-the-end-of-june-2023/); `Summary:` Levada reported that the June 24 mutiny caused only limited short-term movement in attitudes, and Putin’s approval remained high, with the July 2023 table showing 69% approve / 23% disapprove. This is favorable evidence on regime durability and personal standing. `Question IDs:` `7A`, `8B`.

6. **Putin still convened regional leaders at year-end**. `Publisher:` President of Russia / Kremlin; `Date:` 26 Dec 2023; `URL:` [en.special.kremlin.ru/catalog/keywords/82/events/73171](https://en.special.kremlin.ru/catalog/keywords/82/events/73171); `Summary:` The Kremlin reported Putin hosting an informal CIS heads-of-state meeting in St. Petersburg with leaders from Azerbaijan, Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan. This suggests he retained active regional diplomatic reach despite the war and isolation. `Question IDs:` `4A`, `7A`.

## Bottom Line

The best 2023 evidence is mixed but asymmetric: Putin remained in control and still had domestic approval, macroeconomic resilience, and regional diplomatic activity, while 2023 also brought major negative signals from the ICC, the Wagner mutiny, and a sustained crackdown on dissent and civil society.
